title: 200 Million Patient Interactions Later — Vivek Muppalla, Hippocratic AI
talk_summary: Hippocratic AI describes a vertically integrated voice-agent stack (Polaris) that runs 31 specialist models in parallel per conversation, each short-circuiting if it has nothing to contribute, plus background verifier models for tool calls. They emphasize that most apparent reasoning failures are actually ASR mishearing, and that they use domain context to bias transcription and a secondary scoring pass for single-word patient responses.

takeaways.technique: Parallel specialist models with short-circuit gating
takeaways.what_they_do: Run all specialist models in parallel, but each does a fast check whether it needs to speak; if not it short-circuits, keeping latency budget while adding redundancy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single model does a really quick check to see if they even need to say something on this conversation

takeaways.technique: Background verifier models for tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Asynchronous verifier models run in the background checking tool-call parameters and responses for accuracy, separate from the main reasoning model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have these like verifiers in the background that are running to make sure all the parameters into the tool calls and the responses

takeaways.what_they_do: Feed conversation context and domain knowledge (medications, task, policy) into the ASR model so it picks from a finite candidate list rather than guessing from an infinite one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we aren't guessing from like an infinite list of medications, but we have the chance to optimize around a finite list
takeaways.numbers: >50% reduction in medical word error rate

takeaways.technique: Statistical eval sizing + human-in-the-loop at scale
takeaways.what_they_do: Compute how many tests are needed to detect a given failure rate (450 tests for 99% confidence on 1% error), and combine synthetic data with thousands of trained human evaluators because synthetic alone can't reach the needed scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You need about 450 tests to be 99% sure that you can catch this like 1% error rate
takeaways.numbers: 450 tests for 99% confidence on 1% error; 1900 tests to catch it 10 times; 7000 clinicians, ~800k conversations

takeaways.technique: Lossless inference optimizations as a routing constraint
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat quality as a hard constraint and speed as the objective; only adopt lossless optimizations (4-bit quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache compression) and reinvest saved latency in more intelligence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: quality is our constraint, and speed is the work. So, we can never compromise on the quality of the output.

takeaways.technique: Single model as single point of failure — redundancy by design
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly architect around the assumption that any one model will fail, using multiple models so the patient never notices a failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we see a singular model being as like one point of failure, and that's just unacceptable for a patient conversation
